LLM_description:
Situation:
Supply Depot Bravo and Logistics Hub Delta are supporting multiple forward elements, including Forward Operating Base Alpha and subordinate maneuver and fires units operating along the eastern corridor. Combat tempo has increased consumption of critical munitions and POL, with medical and sustainment commodities also required to maintain tempo and readiness. The ground network includes valley routes vulnerable to indirect fire and IEDs, desert tracks with limited cover and austere refuel points, and urban approaches prone to choke points and civil traffic interference. Airlift is constrained by lane availability and weather, so ground convoys are the primary distribution method. Security assets, engineering teams, and EW support are available but limited and must be prioritized.

Mission:
Deliver required supplies from depots to supported units over the operational period while minimizing total operational cost, including transport, shortage penalties, vehicle deployment, and fixed route security risk costs.

Execution/Concept:
- Depots will push multi-supply shipments to supported units by day. Outbound throughput from each depot is limited by available stocks and cannot exceed on-hand quantities. Unit demands must be met; any shortfalls will be recorded as controlled shortages and penalized.
- Convoy sizing will be determined by vehicle capacity and the volumetric footprint of each supply. Heavier or bulkier items consume more capacity and will drive vehicle requirements.
- Vehicles can only move on routes that have been formally activated for that day. Activating any route—sending any vehicles at all—incurs a fixed Risk Cost representing security overhead (escort teams, route clearance, overwatch, and EW support), regardless of the number of vehicles ultimately dispatched on that route.
- Total vehicles employed across all depots and routes on a given day cannot exceed fleet availability. Priority will be given to units at highest operational risk or with critical consumption.
- Transport costs vary by depot-to-unit pairing based on distance, terrain, and threat profile. The plan will minimize the number of activated routes while meeting demands, consolidate loads where feasible, and favor lower-cost lanes when security and timeline permit.
- If constraints prevent full delivery, shortages will be deliberately allocated to least-critical supply types and locations to reduce penalty exposure while preserving mission-essential readiness.

LLM_description_template:
1. Situation:
Task Force Orion must sustain dispersed combat elements in a contested sector while maintaining tempo. Stocks are staged at Supply Depot Bravo and Logistics Hub Delta for onward movement to forward elements including 3rd Infantry Battalion at FOB Arrow, a cavalry troop at COP Ridge, and a fires battery at Fire Base Kodiak. Primary ground routes include a valley corridor exposed to enemy interdiction and a mountain pass constrained by terrain and weather. Movement requires convoy security, route clearance, and ISR coordination. Depot throughput and daily availability of critical supplies are limited. Transport costs and route security risks vary by origin-destination and by day.

2. Mission:
Deliver critical supplies to all designated forward units across the planning horizon, minimizing total operational cost (transport, shortage penalties, vehicle deployment, and fixed route security risk costs) while preserving combat readiness and freedom of maneuver.

3. Execution/Concept:
- Supply allocation:
  - Push priority stocks from Supply Depot Bravo and Logistics Hub Delta to meet unit demands each day. Depot issues are constrained by available supply at each depot by day.
  - Shortfalls may be accepted only where operational risk is manageable; any unmet demand incurs a penalty cost.
- Movement control and fleet:
  - Each vehicle has a fixed carrying capacity; loaded volume/weight of all supplies per convoy leg must not exceed total capacity of vehicles assigned to that leg and day.
  - Total vehicles deployed across all routes on any day cannot exceed fleet availability.
  - Each vehicle deployed carries an associated deployment cost.
- Route activation and risk:
  - A route from a specific depot to a specific unit on a given day must be activated before any vehicles can move on it.
  - Activating a route (sending any vehicles) incurs a fixed Risk Cost representing security overhead (escort teams, route clearance, ISR), charged once per route-day regardless of the number of vehicles.
  - Consolidate shipments to reduce the number of activated routes where feasible without degrading priority resupply.
- Cost and prioritization:
  - Transport costs differ by depot-unit pair and by day; combine these with fixed Risk Costs and vehicle deployment costs to identify the least-cost mix of movements.
  - Weigh shortage penalties against high-risk or high-cost movements to determine acceptable shortfalls without compromising critical operations.
- Command and control:
  - The Movement Control Team will sequence convoys, align escort and clearance assets, and deconflict routes to minimize exposure while meeting daily priorities.
  - Adjustments will be made daily based on depot stock posture, route conditions, and unit consumption.
